content:
Congratulations on the release. This is very interesting to see.

There is a fair amount of overlap with the GameTheory-in-Lean work I have been developing:
https://github.com/elazarg/GameTheory
Especially around strategic games, equilibrium notions, auctions, social choice, matching, zero-sum games, and extensive-form games. The projects seem to have somewhat different design centers, but enough shared scope that coordination would probably be useful.

In particular, it would be good to compare core abstractions, theorem statements, and module boundaries early, so that we can avoid duplicating effort where possible and identify places where one project can reuse, cross-reference, or inform the other. I would be happy to discuss this and help produce a comparison/coordination map.

Great to see this announcement! I've already chatted with Xiaohui Bei and his team, and we had a funny coincidence: his team and mine both concurrently/independently started a project called EconCSLib. Mine is available here: https://github.com/nikhgarg/EconCSLib.

Our motivation is complementary to Xiaohui Bei's EconCSLib -- to formalize research papers, with primarily an AI-first approach aimed at onboarding researchers who do not know Lean, to autoformalize their own papers in a trustworthy-enough manner.

Happy to discuss with everyone here on potential coordination!

Nice to meet you all, I have been formalizing algorithmic game theory on and off since 2024. I noticed that one of the two papers cites our EFX counterexample result. A tiny fraction of the formalization for that paper comes from one of my mathlib PRs. Glad to assist in any way. I am already incorporating algorithmic models for game theory in my framework for algorithms, including the Robertson Webb cake cutting model. Hopefully we can merge and reuse each others work as suitable.
One small note: We usually discuss largely AI authored projects in the #AI authored projects channel.
Thanks! I'll perhaps start a thread there
